Superhydrophilic (SHPi) surfaces have an apparent water contact angle close to 0 degrees, while superhydrophobic (SHPo) surfaces have a contact angle larger than 150 degrees.
The authors fabricate six types of surfaces: hydrophilic, hydrophobic, SHPi, SHPo, biphilic (combining hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions), and superbiphilic (combining SHPi and SHPo regions).
Nucleation on SHPo surfaces occurs at superheats about 2 orders of magnitude lower than on hydrophilic surfaces.
The maximum heat transfer coefficient (HTC) of the biphilic surfaces is 2-4 times higher than the hydrophilic and hydrophobic surfaces, respectively.
Biphilic surfaces combine the advantages of hydrophilic and hydrophobic regions, generating large bubbles while also offering more nucleation sites at low superheats.
The size of the hydrophobic spots on the biphilic surface affects the HTC, with smaller 50 μm spots outperforming larger 400 μm spots at high superheats.
The superbiphilic surfaces exhibit exceptional performance, with critical heat fluxes over 100 W/cm^2 and HTCs over 100 kW/m^2K.
The authors develop an analytical model based on the Mikic and Rohsenow micro-convection theory to describe the HTC on these surfaces.
The model incorporates the measured density of active nucleation sites, bubble departure diameter, and bubble departure frequency for each surface type.
The model and experimental results show good agreement in terms of trends and absolute values of HTC for the different surface types.
Enhancing nucleation on hydrophobic and SHPo surfaces comes with the drawback of reaching critical heat flux at lower heat fluxes due to the formation of an insulating vapor film.
The random nanostructuring process used to fabricate the SHPi surfaces leads to some variation in surface topography and nucleation behavior.
The biphilic surfaces outperform the hydrophilic and hydrophobic surfaces by combining the advantages of both wettability regimes.
The superbiphilic surfaces push the biphilic concept to the extreme, juxtaposing SHPi and SHPo regions for exceptional boiling performance.
The authors provide the first experimental measurements of nucleation site density on SHPi and SHPo surfaces, an important parameter for modeling boiling on these surfaces.
